# Harbor clearance review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Typed pointer visit and injected function callbacks; acquired capability uses pointer identity, never document-key equality.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: Two or more edits less than 120 ms apart produce no early write; 120 ms after the last edit, exactly one write occurs with that edit's exact text.
A later edit before expiry cancels/restarts the prior timer rather than allowing the earlier deadline to write.
After one burst is saved, a later independent burst schedules and saves normally.
An empty string is retained as a valid pending value and written at expiry.
Opening or closing a visit does not redirect an already accepted edit to another document.
Submit remains synchronous and uses the current visit's in-memory text, including edits whose delayed persistence has not yet occurred.

Opening, closing, confirmation display, store subscriptions, and disposal retain their existing externally observable behavior except where delayed edit persistence necessarily changes store-write timing.
Preview queries still publish after 40 ms, hide still cancels unpublished preview work, and later preview queries remain usable.
forbidden_effects: Do not write on every Edit call.
Do not write an older value after a newer edit has restarted the quiet interval.
Do not use truthiness to detect pending text; an empty string is valid.
Do not let navigation cause delayed work from one visit to write to the newly selected document.
Do not make open, edit, close, submit, dispose, or injected interfaces asynchronous.
Do not alter the adjacent search preview or its 40 ms behavior.
Do not change public APIs, injected interface shapes, confirmation ownership semantics, or queue submission receipts.
Do not change tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each Open call creates a fresh *Visit identity, even when reopening the same document ID.
A trailing save belongs to the visit/document for which its task was constructed; document-key equality does not substitute for visit identity where pointer identity is required.
A Confirmation acquires the visit current when BindConfirmation is called and is active only while that same pointer remains current.
Retirement clears the current visit and detaches that visit's store subscription before publishing the empty document output.

obligations.text: Workspace.Edit must continue to update the selected visit's in-memory text synchronously, but must enqueue that exact text through the existing trailing-task utility instead of writing it immediately.
The editor trailing task must use a 120 ms delay measured from the latest edit in the current burst; every later edit before expiry replaces the pending text and restarts the interval.
At expiry, exactly the latest text from that burst must be written once to the document ID captured for the originating visit.
After a burst is consumed, the same editor behavior must remain reusable so subsequent bursts can be saved.
Valid empty text must be preserved and written; only the utility's existing nil pending sentinel denotes absence of work.
Delayed persistence must not change the synchronous signatures or return behavior of open, edit, close, submit, dispose, or the injected interfaces.

Submit must continue to capture the currently selected visit's in-memory id and text, return the queue receipt synchronously, return nil when no editor is selected, and show confirmation only through the capability acquired for the still-current visit.

Existing navigation behavior must remain: each opening creates a fresh visit, persisted text is restored, the prior store subscription is stopped on retirement, and delayed work must never be redirected to another document.
The Preview implementation and its 40 ms trailing behavior are outside this change and must remain unchanged.
Dispose must retain the documented ordering in which integrations are detached before the workspace is closed.

ordering_barriers: On Edit, update Visit.text before scheduling its delayed persistence so synchronous Submit observes the latest accepted text.
On each trailing Push, cancel the prior handle before scheduling the replacement deadline.
On trailing Flush, capture the pending text and retire the batch's handle/pending state before invoking Write; callback-capable work cannot erase or consume a later batch.
On visit retirement, clear current authority and stop the leaving visit's store subscription before emitting the empty document state.
On Submit, acquire confirmation ownership for the current visit, form the snapshot from that visit, synchronously capture it, then show the receipt only if that acquired visit remains current.
On Dispose, detach integrations before performing close behavior.

Submit returns its receipt, or nil when no editor is selected.
Confirmation capability continues to use pointer identity rather than document-key equality.
Store status publication and document/notice outputs retain their existing behavior except for the required delay and coalescing of edit-triggered writes.
Search preview retains its 40 ms quiet interval, cancellation on hide, and later reuse.
Exact text values, including the empty string, are preserved.

The supplied trailing utility cancels the prior handle, replaces pending text, clears batch state before invoking work, accepts empty strings through a pointer sentinel, and is reusable after Flush. Syntax passed. The bare failed acceptance verdict supplies no normative requirement and no failure cause, so it cannot establish either an implementation gap or a behavioral contract gap. The behavioral contract is therefore preserved unchanged.

routing_analysis.contract: Edit persistence is a reusable deferred trailing batch scoped to the visit created by Open: every accepted edit synchronously changes the visit snapshot, replaces the batch value, and restarts a 120 ms timer; expiry consumes the batch before writing its latest exact text to the document ID captured when the visit task was created. Navigation, submission, confirmation ownership, subscriptions, disposal ordering, synchronous APIs, and the independent 40 ms preview behavior remain preserved. Public sources leave the precise pending-edit policy at navigation/disposal boundaries and timer reentrancy/race semantics unspecified.
